changes: First Modwerk import of Bryan T's LOFI2 from octabam: a ring modulator or stereo frequency shifter (MODE RING / DOWN / UP), then sample-rate and bit reduction on stock LO-FI's curves and a high-shelf cut. Stock LO-FI stays in the chooser beside it.
Upstream implementation, unchanged: the DSP is the author's optimised revision (octabam pull request 704, merged 13 October 2026; 416 cycles/sample in SHIFT, down from 654).

Modwerk packaging: effect ID 0x09 instead of octabam's 0x1f (TapeHead's here), so a project saved with octabam's LOFI2 does not select it; the range select is named RNGE and MODE keeps its own name on the SETUP page; with stock DSP code built in it takes the space of two adjacent stock reverbs, and it cannot be combined with Analog BD.

Over USB the Modwerk base loads LOFI2 on demand into FX1 or FX2. It declares 637 cycles a sample, timed on an MKII, so two instances fit on one DSP core when its other slots are free and a third is refused (DSP FULL).

Limits: SHIFT costs about 1.4x stock SPRING REV per instance and is dearer than every stock effect. In DOWN and UP a faint residue (about -77 dBFS) stays after the input stops. Hardware: one short functional run on an MKII on the exact card image (every mode, five SHIFT instances, a FREQ lock, a Part reload and a power cycle passed), and a run of the USB package on the beta base (FX1 and FX2 on both cores, two instances on one core, Keep and Undo, removal, the missing-module fallback, project reload and a power cycle). Eight instances and scenes are untested. The author reports the same loop running on his MKII, eight instances at once, in his own build.
